## How We Work: Our Company Values

Three company values guide every job: a quality-first approach , close customer focus and a sustainable process . At Koojo Custom Powder Coating they are practical rules, not slogans, and they decide how we prepare, coat and check each part.
Quality first
We use quality powders, prepare every surface properly and test the finish before release. Our checks are set out on the powder coating quality assurance page.
Customer focus

We listen first, then confirm colour, prep and timing before work starts, so nothing on your order is left to guesswork. Ask any repeat customer about us and this is usually the first thing they mention.
A sustainable process
Powder coating produces far less waste than many liquid finishes, and overspray can often be collected. We plan loads to make good use of each oven cycle.

## What Is Powder Coating?

Powder coating is a dry finishing process. Thermoset powder is sprayed onto clean, grounded metal with an electrostatic gun, then cured in an oven at roughly 180 to 200 °C. The heat melts the powder into one continuous film that is harder and more chip-resistant than most liquid paints, with no solvents released.

As a powder coating company GTA businesses rely on for repeat work, we focus on what decides how long a finish lasts: surface preparation, correct film thickness and a full cure. Our guides on what is powder coating and powder coating vs wet paint go deeper.

## Our Powder Coating Process
Every order follows the same five steps. Our step-by-step powder coating process guide explains each one in detail.
### Quote & Inspect
We review your photos, drawings or parts, then confirm price, colour and ready date in writing.
### Strip & Blast
Old coatings, rust and mill scale are removed, leaving a clean, profiled surface the powder can grip.
### Pretreat & Mask
Parts are degreased and phosphate-treated, and threads, holes and contact faces are plugged or taped.
### Coat & Cure
Powder is applied electrostatically, then cured at about 180 to 200 °C into one hard, continuous film.
### Inspect & Hand Over
We test adhesion and thickness, check colour and coverage, then pack parts for pickup or delivery.

## What to Send for an Accurate Price
Send part measurements , part quantity , the metal, the finish you want and one or two photos. With those five details we can usually price a job straight away, without a follow-up call.

Measure the longest length, the widest point and the height, including anything that sticks out. For the colour, give the colour code if you have one, such as a RAL number, or describe the look you want and we will suggest options. Note any masking requirements , such as threads, mounting faces or contact points that must stay bare. If the part has old paint or rust, mention it, because removal changes the powder coating estimate . For unusual or very heavy items, a sample part or a drawing helps us give a firm figure rather than a range. The more complete your request, the faster and more accurate your quote will be. A complete powder coating quote request rarely needs a second round of questions, and that keeps your job moving.

## What Affects the Price

Five price factors shape every powder coating quote : the size of the part, the prep it needs, the quantity, the colour and finish, and the amount of masking. Two parts that look alike can cost different amounts for these reasons.

That is why your quote is always written for your exact part. Heavy rust or old coatings add blasting or stripping time. Large items use more oven space, while a batch of matching parts spreads setup across many pieces. Special colours or textures can cost more than stock shades, and detailed masking takes extra labour. For typical price ranges and what drives them, read our guide to powder coating cost . They are ten connected metal finishing services that take a part from rust, scale or old paint to a cured, tested finish. Some jobs need one step, others need several, and we combine them into a single order.

Powder coating itself is a dry powder sprayed by electrostatic spray and hardened by oven curing , which gives protective coatings that resist chips, fading and corrosion better than many liquid paints. Around that core sit the supporting coating services : surface preparation, blasting, colour work, stripping and recoating, plus specialist work for vehicles, wheels, buildings, volume orders and one-off pieces. Abrasive & Mobile Sandblasting
Blasting removes rust, mill scale and old coatings, in the shop or on site, leaving a clean profile the powder can grip.
Cleaning & Phosphate Pretreatment
Degreasing and pretreatment prepare the metal so the powder bonds firmly, then parts are rinsed and fully dried. Pretreatment also slows corrosion under the coating if the finish is ever damaged.
Masking & Plugging
Masking and plugging protect threads, mounting faces and contact points. Plugs and high-temperature tape come off after curing, leaving clean edges.

Charged powder wraps around edges and into corners for even coverage, the core of our service range . Film build is kept even so colour and gloss match across every part in a batch.
Oven Curing
Parts cure at 180–200 °C until the metal itself reaches temperature, so thick sections cure fully. Curing time follows the powder maker's data sheet, not guesswork.
Quality Inspection & DFT Check
Quality inspection covers film thickness, adhesion, colour and coverage before release. Results are recorded, so test reports can go out with any of our coating services on request.
Packaging & Shipping
Packaging and shipping protect finished faces, and the job ends with pickup or delivery. Finished faces are wrapped so they arrive exactly as they left inspection, the final step of every service .

## Will My Part Fit?

Your part will usually fit if it is shorter than 23 ft, inside the oven's width and height, under 6,000 lb, and has somewhere solid to hang or support it. Check those four points first, then send us the part dimensions for a final yes.

Measure the longest length, the widest point and the tallest point, including anything that sticks out. Add the weight if you know it, or the steel size and length so we can estimate it. Long parts such as beams, rails and structural steel members fit lengthwise, so length is rarely the issue for large parts ; width, height and hanging points usually decide. If a part is close to a limit, photos of the welds and lifting points help us plan large part powder coating without surprises on delivery day.
## Equipment and Process for Big Work

Big parts follow the same steps as small ones, but each step is planned around size and mass: blasting, pretreatment and masking, then electrostatic coating and a full cure in our large curing oven . Planning comes first, because large parts cannot be reworked cheaply.
Blasting

In-house blasting removes mill scale, rust and old coatings so the powder bonds to clean metal, and mobile sandblasting covers items that are too awkward to move. That step matters most in large part powder coating , where a missed patch is hard to fix later. Learn more about our sandblasting services .
Pretreatment and Masking
Chemical pretreatment improves adhesion and corrosion resistance, and masking protects threads, mounting faces and contact points. Our powder coating surface preparation page explains each step.
Coating and Curing

Electrostatic spraying wraps powder around big frames and into corners. The 23 ft oven then cures each piece at 180–200 °C, and heavy sections stay in until the metal itself reaches temperature, which is what keeps a consistent finish on powder coating for large parts .
## What We Coat at This Size

Typical large parts include equipment frames , conveyor and automation structures, machine bases, structural steel, railings and gates, trailer and vehicle frames, and heavy machinery coating for plant upgrades. Small parts can ride along in the same order.

Our industrial powder coating page covers the full service for heavy frames and machinery, and our powder coating projects page shows finished examples with specs and photos. Both are good places to see how parts of this size come out, and how the same quality carries from a single beam to a full skid of large parts bound for a new production line.
## From One-Off Jobs to Recurring Volume

We handle one-off and repeat orders with the same care. A single oversized frame gets its own planned cycle, while batch coating suits repeat runs of matching parts, and recurring bulk work can be scheduled to suit your production calendar.

Customers with steady volume often book oven time ahead, which keeps large part powder coating on a predictable rhythm. For pricing and account options on volume work, see commercial powder coating , which covers recurring orders in detail. Batch work also makes it easier to keep colour matched across large parts made months apart, and recorded colour codes make later reorders simple.
## Quality on Every Big Part

Large parts get the same checks as small ones. We measure film thickness to ASTM D7091 across faces, edges and welds, test adhesion to ASTM D3359, and record the results, so a 20 ft frame meets the same standard as a bracket.
Readings are taken where big parts fail first: long welds, outside corners and the lowest edge of the hang.

Our quality system is certified by the Absolute Bureau of Certification, and test reports are available on request. The steps are set out on our powder coating quality assurance page, which applies to powder coating large parts as well as everyday work.

body: Specialty powder coating gives unusual parts, test pieces and art pieces a tough, even finish that suits the job instead of forcing it into a standard run. At Koojo Custom Powder Coating, our Milton team coats single pieces and small sets with the same care as large orders. Since 2012, we have finished more than 10,000 items for customers across the GTA, with a 48-hour turnaround on typical orders. Whether you need one-off powder coating for a sculpture or a repair, we plan every step around your part. Call (905) 876-7060, Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, or request a specialty powder coating quote below.
Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | 48 Hr Turnaround | Google Rating
## What Is Specialty Powder Coating ?

Specialty powder coating is a dry finishing process for unusual, one-off or custom metal parts, in which electrostatically charged powder is sprayed onto the part and heated in an oven until it cures into a hard, even layer. It suits work that does not fit a standard production run.

The finish is made from thermoset powder , which cures with heat instead of drying like liquid paint. At a cure temperature of 180 to 200 °C , the powder flows, bonds to the metal and hardens into one continuous coating without runs or drips. That makes it a dependable corrosion-resistant and chip-resistant choice for parts that face weather, handling and wear. As a form of specialty metal finishing , it is often chosen where a part is hard to replace.

Typical projects include one-off parts , test builds, custom fabrications and decorative metalwork , along with metal sculptures from artists and makers. Good one-off powder coating depends on planning each job from the bare metal up, so our specialty powder coating is planned around the part in front of us, not a standard recipe. Our wider powder coating services cover the full range of work we do.
## Our Specialty Powder Coating Process

Our specialty powder coating process has six stages: intake and inspection, cleaning and pretreatment , masking, powder application, oven curing and final inspection. Each stage is documented, so a repeat of your project matches the first piece. The same controls support our industrial powder coating work.

Step 1 – Intake and Inspection

We check each part for rust, old coatings, weld seams and damage, then confirm the finish and your timing. Unusual shapes are studied first, because hanging a part so every surface can be reached is often the hardest step on a single job.
Step 2 – Cleaning and Pretreatment

Parts are washed and chemically treated so the powder bonds to clean metal. Skipping this stage is a common reason finishes fail early. Parts that need old coatings removed first may suit our powder coat stripping and recoating service.
Step 3 – Masking and Plugging
Threaded holes , bearing surfaces and mounting points are protected before coating. Masking and plugging keep bolts turning and parts fitting, which matters when there is only one part and no spare.
Step 4 – Electrostatic Powder Application

Charged powder is applied by electrostatic spray onto the grounded part, so it wraps around tubes, corners and recesses. This helps even coverage on irregular shapes that a flat panel recipe would miss.
Step 5 – Oven Curing

The part moves into the curing oven , where specialty powder coating reaches temperature and hardens. Cure time depends on the powder and the mass of the part, so a heavy casting is planned differently from a thin decorative piece.
Step 6 – Final Inspection and Handoff

We inspect the cured finish for coverage, adhesion and appearance. Typical orders are ready within 48 hours, and unusual jobs are scheduled when we quote. We receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. We also record the colour code and powder used, so a later piece can match.
Our small-batch powder coating schedule keeps parts from waiting between steps, and for a tight lead time , tell us your date at quote.
## Parts and Metals We Coat

We apply specialty powder coating to steel, aluminum and cast parts, including test parts, brackets, decorative panels, sculptures and welded assemblies. Our capabilities page lists 6,000 lb capacity, so heavy pieces, long frames and odd shapes are all worth a quote, and we confirm fit at intake.
 One-off parts : replacement pieces, repairs and single custom items.

Architectural powder coating is a finishing process in which dry, electrostatically charged powder is sprayed onto prepared building metalwork and cured in an oven. It forms a hard, even shell that protects the steel and aluminum parts used on and around buildings.

Unlike liquid paint, powder has no solvent carrier. The charged particles cling to the metal, then melt and cross-link in the oven, typically at 180 to 200 °C. restoration-recoating.summary: Powder Coat Stripping and Recoating for Metal Parts
body: Powder coat stripping and recoating removes a failed, damaged or unwanted finish and replaces it with a fresh powder coat finish that bonds to clean metal. At Koojo Custom Powder Coating in Milton, we have finished more than 10,000 items since 2012, and many of them were older parts brought back into service. Whether your railings are peeling, your frames are chipped or your equipment has rusted, our powder coat removal and recoating service restores the metal and its protection. Tell us what the part is and what is wrong with it, and we will recommend the right approach.

Our standard turnaround is 48 hours for typical shop orders, and we are open Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Heavily rusted or multi-part jobs are scheduled when we quote, once we know the size, the condition and how much old coating removal the parts need. Every powder coat stripping and recoating job starts with a short conversation about the part and what went wrong.
Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | 48 Hr Turnaround | Google Rating
## What Is Powder Coat Stripping and Recoating?

Powder coat stripping and recoating is a two-part restoration process. The old finish comes off completely, then new powder is applied electrostatically and cured in an oven. The goal is a clean, even finish that bonds to bare metal instead of a new layer sitting on a failing one.

Powder coat recoating over a damaged finish rarely lasts. A peeling powder coat or a chipped powder coating usually means the bond has already failed, and a new coat on top can lift in the same places. Rust under the surface makes this worse, because it keeps spreading beneath any new film. That is why we remove the old finish first and complete surface rust treatment before the new powder goes on.

Not every part needs full powder coating restoration . A faded powder coat on a sound surface may only need cleaning and a refresh, while rust, damage or a colour change calls for complete old coating removal . We assess each part before we quote, so powder coat stripping and recoating covers only the work the part actually needs.
## How Our Powder Coat Stripping and Recoating Process Works

Our powder coat stripping and recoating process has six stages: assessment, removal, rust repair , pretreatment, recoating and inspection. Each stage protects the next one, so the new finish bonds properly and lasts.

Assessment. We look at the metal, the existing coating, the extent of rust and any damage. Photos sent with your quote request help us plan the stripping and recoating , including the removal method, the repairs and the finish, before the part arrives.

Removal. We take the old finish down to bare metal. Paint stripping and powder coat stripping take different effort, so we confirm the method for your part when we quote. Heavy coatings, scale and rust often call for blasting,
described on our sandblasting services page.

Rust repair. Surface rust is cleaned from the metal so it cannot spread under the new coat. Deep pitting or structural damage is flagged to you early, because recoating cannot restore a weakened part.

Pretreatment. Clean metal can develop flash rust quickly, so pretreatment before recoating follows removal closely. Our surface preparation page explains the washing and masking steps, and surface preparation for recoating is part of every restoration job.
Recoating. We plug threads and bores, then apply the powder electrostatically. Oven curing at 180–200 °C melts the powder into one continuous film.
Inspection. We check coverage, colour and finish, measure film thickness and look for defects before packing the part.

Timing matters as much as technique. Typical shop work follows our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Planning powder coat stripping and recoating as one job keeps bare metal from sitting uncoated, which is the main cause of early flash rust. Recoating turnaround for larger or heavily rusted parts is confirmed when we quote. Parts with several layers of old paint can take longer to strip, so we ask for photos early.
## Which Parts and Metals Can We Restore?

Our stripping and recoating service covers steel and aluminum parts that can withstand curing, from small brackets to large fabricated frames. See our capabilities page for size and weight limits. Typical jobs include:
Railings and gates. Railing restoration and gate restoration are common, because outdoor metalwork loses its finish first.
Equipment and machinery. Equipment refurbishment and machinery refurbishment bring worn housings, guards and frames back to a protected finish.
Structural steel and frames. Structural steel recoating suits fabricated frames and supports where rust has started under the old coat.
Older metalwork. Aging metalwork from churches, parks and buildings often carries several layers of old paint, which we remove before recoating.

Galvanized, cast and heavily welded parts can need extra checks because trapped gases may affect the surface, so tell us the material when you request a quote. Some parts are not worth restoring, and we will say so if the metal is too weak or too damaged. For parts that live outdoors, powder coat stripping and recoating helps restore weathered metal and extend coating life .
## Restoration and Recoating Options
You can return a part to its original look or change it completely. The stripping and recoating options below cover the most common requests, and each can be paired with a new finish.
Like-for-like recoating. We aim for an original colour match so the restored part blends with the rest of the installation. Send a colour code, a RAL number or a small sample.
Colour change recoating. A new shade, sheen or texture gives older parts a new look. Our custom powder coating colours page explains the choices.
Removal with repair. Some parts need old coating removal and rust repair before they return to service. Tell us what is wrong and we will confirm the steps.
Repair or recoat. A small chip may be repairable, but widespread peeling, rust or fading means a full recoat is the better choice. We tell you which applies when we assess the part.

Not sure whether your part needs stripping at all? Send photos with your quote request. A restoration quote for powder coat stripping and recoating starts with a clear description of the damage and the finish you want, and it lets us refinish metal parts without guesswork. Whatever you choose, we confirm the plan with you before work starts.
## How We Check Restoration Quality

For every powder coat stripping and recoating job, we check the bare metal after removal, then the finished coat, before parts leave the shop. Our quality steps are outlined on our certification page, and test reports are available on request.

Where a job calls for it, test methods include the ASTM D3359 adhesion test , ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance. Our certification is held through the Absolute Bureau of Certification. A new finish is only worth applying if it stays bonded, so we test adhesion as well as appearance on powder coat recoating work, which helps prevent a repeat adhesion failure or coating failure . We also confirm the cured finish is even, with no thin spots, runs or bare patches.
## Restoration in Practice

Our church gates project shows how Koojo documents architectural metalwork from first inspection to the finished coat. The case study lists the part, metal, size, powder, colour code and turnaround, with before and after photos , so you can see how stripping and recoating work is recorded.

You can also browse more finished parts on our Our Work page. A good restoration brief includes the part, the metal, what is wrong and the finish you want. With those four details, we can quote powder coat stripping and recoating accurately and confirm the plan before work begins.
## Who Uses Our Recoating Service

## Municipal and institutional owners, contractors, farm and heavy equipment owners and manufacturers use our powder coat stripping and recoating service most. These customers have metal that has aged, and they need a durable finish back quickly, with a clear scope and a documented result.

See how we support municipal and institutional customers with bollards, park equipment and church metalwork, and agricultural and heavy equipment owners, where rust is the main concern. Our powder coat stripping and recoating also supports our wider industrial powder coating work and the full range of powder coating services at our Milton shop.
## Get Your Metal Restored

Ready to bring worn metal back to a lasting finish? Send part photos and details through our quote form for powder coat stripping and recoating advice, or visit 10874 Steeles Ave E, Milton, Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Call (905) 876-7060 or email sales@koojopowdercoating.com.
faqs: Can you remove old powder coating from my part?

Yes. Our powder coat stripping takes the finish down to bare metal, then we check the surface and recoat it. Send photos and part details with your quote request so we can confirm the removal method and any repairs.
Is it better to repair a chip or recoat the whole part?

A small chip may be repairable, but widespread chipping, peeling or rust means a full recoat is the better choice. A new coat on top of a failing one tends to lift again, so we advise stripping and recoating with a bare metal finish first.
Do you treat rust before recoating?
Yes. We clean surface rust from the metal so it cannot spread under the new coat. Deep pitting or structural damage is flagged early, because recoating cannot restore a weakened part.
Can I change the colour when I recoat?
Yes. A recoat is a good time to choose a new colour, sheen or texture. Send a RAL number or sample and we will confirm what is available when we quote.
How long does powder coat stripping and recoating take?
Typical shop orders follow our standard 48-hour turnaround. Large, heavily rusted or multi-part jobs are scheduled when we quote, once we know the size, condition and amount of removal.
What should I send for a restoration quote?
Send photos of the part, its size and quantity, a description of the problem and the colour you want. This lets us price powder coat stripping and recoating accurately.

body: Sandblasting services remove rust, scale and old surface contamination so bare metal is ready for a lasting powder coat. At Koojo Custom Powder Coating, our Milton team uses abrasive blasting in the shop and offers mobile sandblasting for parts and structures that cannot travel. Since 2012, we have finished more than 10,000 items for fabricators, manufacturers and contractors across the GTA, with a 48-hour turnaround on shop work. Whether you have welded frames, aging railings or heavy equipment, we match the blasting method to the metal and the finish you want. Request a sandblasting quote below, or call (905) 876-7060, Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, to talk through your project. Careful sandblasting before powder coating keeps the finish bonded for years.
Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | 48 Hr Turnaround | Google Rating
## What Are Sandblasting Services ?

Sandblasting services use compressed air to drive abrasive media against metal, removing rust, scale and old surface debris. The result is clean, bare metal with an even texture that lets powder coating grip firmly and last for years, even in tough outdoor conditions.

The word sandblasting is common, but most modern work uses other abrasives, so the broader names are media blasting and abrasive blasting . Each media cuts differently. Aluminum oxide blasting and steel grit blasting cut fast and leave a rougher surface, while glass bead blasting leaves a smoother, cleaner finish. The texture left behind is called the surface profile , or anchor profile , and it gives powder something to hold. Good blast cleaning removes everything that would stop a coating from bonding and leaves a bare metal finish ready to coat.

That is why we treat industrial sandblasting as part of the coating process, not a separate chore. Sandblasting and powder coating work best when one team plans both, because clean steel starts to show flash rust soon after blasting. Skipping this link in the chain is the most common reason a coating fails early.
## How Does Our Sandblasting Process Work?

Our sandblasting services follow five stages: inspection, blast media selection , blasting, cleanup, and handoff to coating. Each stage protects the metal and the finish, and blasted parts move to coating quickly so rust never gets a chance to return to the metal before the coating goes on.

Inspection and planning (on arrival). We check each part for heavy rust, pitted and scaled steel , weld spatter and thin sections. We then decide whether the job suits our shop or on-site sandblasting . Early inspection lets us flag problem areas before they cost you time.

Blast media selection . The right media depends on the metal and the finish you need. Tough rust and scale call for harder media, while softer metals and cosmetic parts need gentler options. We confirm the choice with you when the finish or tolerance is critical.

Blasting. Our operators work across every surface, including welds, corners and recesses. They adjust pressure and distance so rust and mill-scale removal is complete without damaging thin sections. Industrial sandblasting at this stage is methodical, never rushed.
Cleanup. Compressed air and brushing clear spent media and dust from holes, seams and enclosed sections. Trapped grit would cause defects under the powder, so we never skip this step.
Inspection and handoff. We confirm a uniform, blast-cleaned surface , then move the part toward coating as soon as possible, since flash rust can form quickly on clean steel.

Timing matters as much as technique. Shop blasting sits inside our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. For mobile sandblasting , tell us the site, access and schedule when you request a quote and we will plan the visit around your deadline. Industrial sandblasting is scheduled alongside coating, so a blasted part never waits long between steps. That planning prevents the gaps that let bare metal rust, and it keeps your project moving.
## Which Metals and Parts Need Sandblasting?

Steel and iron benefit most, because rust and scale form naturally on them. Cast parts, structural steel, fabricated frames and heavy equipment also respond well. Thin or soft metals need gentler media, so our sandblasting services plan the method for each metal before blasting starts.

Steel and iron. Sandblasting steel removes rust and mill scale, the hard grey layer left by hot rolling that blocks coating adhesion. It is the most common job we handle, and it suits everything from small brackets to large frames.
Welded and cast parts. Sandblasting weldments cleans weld discoloration and spatter, and gives rust removal from metal even in tight corners.
Aluminum and softer metals. Gentler media protects the surface, so we choose finer abrasives and lower pressure for these parts, which keeps edges and details sharp.

Typical work includes sandblasting structural steel , sandblasting gates and railings , sandblasting trailers and frames , machine bases and equipment housings. Sandblasting heavy equipment and sandblasting large fabrications can be done in our shop or on site, so confirm the part size when you request a quote. Whether you need sandblasting metal parts one at a time or industrial sandblasting for a full production run, we plan the abrasive blasting to protect the metal.
## What Sandblasting Options Does Koojo Offer?

Koojo offers shop blasting for parts we can move, a mobile service for work on site, and a choice of blast media to suit the metal. Blasting is most often paired with powder coating, so ask us how your job should be planned from start to finish.
Shop sandblasting. Parts come to our Milton shop, where blasting happens in a controlled setting with dust containment and a fast route into coating.

Mobile sandblasting . Our mobile blasting crew brings on-site blasting equipment to structures, large frames and fixed equipment that are hard to move. Portable sandblasting equipment suits these jobs. Share site access and layout when you quote.
Media choices. Blast media selection covers aluminum oxide, steel grit and glass bead, matched to the metal and the finish you want. Larger industrial sandblasting jobs often use a mix of media.

What comes next. After blasting, many parts still need washing and masking, which our powder coating surface preparation service covers. Parts with aged coatings may suit our restoration and recoating service.

Not sure which option fits? Send photos and the part material. We will recommend an approach, and our sandblasting services advice comes with your quote. Choosing the right method up front avoids a damaged part, and protects the rust protection your coating is meant to provide.
## How Do We Check Blasting Quality?

We verify blasting through visual inspection and a surface check before coating. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, our inspection steps are documented, and test reports are available on request, so you can trust the work behind every finish.

Quality starts at intake, when we look for heavy rust, thick scale and old coatings. After blasting, a blast-cleaned surface should look even in colour, with no shiny rust patches, leftover scale or traces of old paint. Surface profile matters too. If the surface is too smooth, powder grips poorly, and if it is too rough, peaks can show through the finish and shorten its life. We check this before parts move on, and we flag any concern with you early.

Our sandblasting services are never signed off until the part passes these checks. Consistent industrial sandblasting also means the next batch matches the last, because we keep records that support repeat orders. Cleanup is part of quality. Loose grit left in seams spoils the coating, so we clear it before parts move on. Because clean bare steel can show flash rust quickly, we plan coating soon after blasting, and we hold shop and mobile work to the same documented checks every time. See our certification page for details on how we work. Careful abrasive blasting also leaves the clean bare steel that strong coatings need.
## See Sandblasting in a Real Project

Outdoor metalwork such as bollards and gates collects rust, scale and old coatings, which makes sandblasting services a smart first step. Our safety bollards case study documents the part, metal, size, powder, colour code and turnaround for a real customer, so you can see what a documented job looks like.

Read the safety bollards project to see the finished result. Before and after photos show the standard we hold ourselves to, from the bare metal stage through to the finished coating, and the same documented approach applies to your parts.
## Which Industries Use Our Sandblasting Services ?

## What Are Custom Powder Coating Colours?

Custom powder coating colours are shades matched to your specification rather than picked from a stock range. The powder is sprayed on electrostatically and cured in an oven, so the colour becomes part of a hard, even finish instead of a thin layer of paint.

Most requests fall into three groups. The first is a standard shade from our powder colour range . The second is RAL colour matching , where you give us a RAL number. The third is a colour match to a sample , where you send us a chip, swatch or small part. Each group changes how we source the powder and how we confirm the result with you. A custom powder coat colour is only as good as its reference, so a clear specification saves time.

Custom powder coat colour is only half of the decision. Sheen levels decide how that colour looks once it is on the part. Gloss powder coating is smooth and bright, matte powder coating cuts glare, and satin powder coating sits in between. The same shade can read very differently in each, so we talk through sheen before we order the powder.
## How We Match and Apply Custom Powder Coating Colours

We confirm your colour reference, prepare the metal, apply the powder electrostatically, cure it at 180–200 °C and inspect the result against your sample. Each step protects the colour match and the finish quality from the first brief to the final check.

Colour brief. Send a RAL number, a RAL colour chart reference, a brand specification or physical colour samples . Samples are best, because screens and printed charts rarely show the true shade. This is where custom colour matching starts.
Powder selection. We check the powder coating colour chart and our supplier range for your shade and finish. If a colour must be ordered in, we confirm the timing with you before work starts.
Surface preparation. Clean metal holds colour evenly. We degrease, remove rust and scale, and pretreat the part where needed, as described on our surface preparation page.
Masking. We plug threads and bores and cover contact points so your custom powder coat colour stays only where you want it.
Spray and cure. The powder is applied electrostatically, then cured in the oven at 180–200 °C. The heat melts the powder and bonds the pigment into one continuous film.
Inspection. We compare the finished custom powder coating colours with your reference, check coverage and thickness, and look for defects before packing.

Some finishes need an extra step. Candy colours and certain effect powders are often built as a two-coat finish , with a coloured base followed by a second layer. This adds time, so we explain it when we quote. For repeat orders, we record the powder and colour code to support batch colour consistency on later runs of your custom powder coating colours . Whether your custom powder coating colours are in stock changes the timing, so we check availability early.
## Which Parts and Metals Can We Colour?

We apply custom powder coating colours to steel and aluminum parts, from small brackets to large fabricated frames. The part must withstand oven curing, so we review each item before quoting. See our capabilities page for size and weight limits.

Typical work includes railings, gates, bollards, machine guards, equipment housings and frames. Powder coating for fabricated parts is a large share of what we do, and one consistent colour across welded assemblies is often the main requirement. Galvanized and cast metals can need extra checks because trapped gases may affect the surface, so tell us the material when you ask for a quote. Send photos with your request so we can check size, weight and masking needs early. Every custom powder coat colour we apply is matched to the metal as well as the specification.

Parts that live outdoors also need the right powder. UV-resistant powder coating holds its colour better in sunlight, which matters for fences, outdoor furniture and building metalwork. For an outdoor-durable finish on exterior products, see our architectural powder coating service, or read our guide to outdoor furniture finishes .
## Finish Options for Your Colour Choice

You can pair any custom powder coat colour with a finish type: gloss, satin, matte, textured, metallic, candy or clear coat. The finish changes how the colour looks, feels and wears, so it is worth choosing both together. These powder coating finishes give you plenty of room to match a design.
Gloss and high-gloss finish. A smooth, reflective surface that is easy to wipe clean.
Satin and low-gloss finish. A softer sheen that shows fewer fingerprints and marks.
Matte. A flat, modern look with the least glare.
Textured powder coating. A wrinkle finish or hammertone finish adds pattern, and an anti-slip textured finish improves grip. Texture also hides surface imperfections such as light weld marks.
Metallic powder coat. Our custom colour powder coating can include silver, bronze and copper metallics that add depth and sparkle.
Candy powder coating. A translucent custom powder coat colour over a base that gives rich colour depth .
Clear coat powder coating. A transparent top layer that protects metallic and candy effects.
Choosing between metallic shades? Our metallic finishes guide explains the differences, and our RAL colour guide shows how RAL numbers translate to powder.

We check your custom powder coat colour against your reference, measure film thickness and test adhesion before parts leave the shop. Where a job calls for it, test methods include ASTM D3359 for adhesion, ASTM D7091 for dry film thickness and ASTM B117 for salt spray resistance. Our certification is held through the Absolute Bureau of Certification. A custom powder coating colour is only useful if it stays attached and even, so we test the finish as well as the shade.
Fade resistance depends on the powder chemistry and the pigment. Bright reds and oranges fade faster outdoors than neutral tones, so we ask where the part will be used before recommending a powder.

Industrial powder coating is a dry, electrostatically applied thermoset finish, cured at roughly 180 to 200 °C and engineered for parts in heavy service rather than for appearance alone. Compared with decorative work, it demands tighter control of surface profile, film thickness and cure, backed by documented testing.

An industrial coating system is chosen for the exposure the part will face: indoor plant floors, washdown areas, outdoor yards or salted roads. That choice sets the blast grade, pretreatment, powder chemistry and whether a primer is needed. Typical parts include machine bases, conveyor frames, structural beams, storage racks, electrical enclosures, safety guards, hoppers, chutes and trailer components. New to the finish itself? Start with our guide on what is powder coating, then come back here for the industrial detail that matters on spec work.

## Our Industrial Powder Coating Process

Every order moves through the same eight controlled steps, from spec review to packed shipment, so results repeat from the first part to the last. Each step is recorded against your drawing, which is how we
meet an industrial coating spec rather than simply a colour.
### Inspection & Spec Review

We check the drawing or spec sheet, metal type, weld quality, part weight and exposure environment, then confirm the powder, colour, film build and any test requirements in writing before work starts.
### Abrasive & Mobile Sandblasting

Rust, mill scale and old coatings are removed by abrasive blasting, leaving a clean, angular profile that meets your specified SSPC or ISO blast grade. Fixed or oversized structures can be blasted on site with our sandblasting services.
### Cleaning & Phosphate Pretreatment

Parts are degreased, rinsed and treated with iron or zinc phosphate to improve adhesion and slow under-film corrosion. Our powder coating surface preparation page explains each chemical stage in more detail.
### Masking & Plugging
Threads, bores, bearing seats, grounding points and mating faces are plugged or taped with high-temperature masking, so they stay bare and fit correctly at assembly.
### Electrostatic Powder Application

Charged powder is sprayed onto the grounded part, wrapping edges and recesses evenly. Primer and topcoat are applied in sequence when a two-coat industrial powder coating system is specified for harsher exposure.
### Oven Curing

Parts are cured to the powder maker's schedule, typically 180 to 200 °C for 10 to 20 minutes at metal temperature, so the film fully cross-links. Thick, heavy sections are given longer soak time to reach temperature.
### Quality Inspection & DFT Check
We measure dry film thickness, run adhesion checks and inspect colour, gloss and coverage on each batch. Readings are recorded for every batch and can be supplied with your order.
### Packaging & Shipping
Finished parts are wrapped, blocked and strapped to protect the powder-coated surface in transit, then shipped or held for pickup at our shop.

faqs: Can you powder coat parts that are already welded or assembled?
Yes, if the assembly can handle cure temperatures of about 200 °C. Rubber, plastic, bearings and electronics must come out first or the oven will damage them.
How thick should an industrial powder coat be?
Most single-coat parts are specified at 2 to 4 mils, and two-coat systems with a primer often run 4 to 6 mils. Our powder coating thickness guide explains the ranges.
Can galvanized steel be powder coated?
Yes, with the right preparation. Galvanized steel is sweep-blasted and often preheated to release trapped gas, which prevents pinholes. Our powder coating galvanized steel guide explains outgassing.

How long does industrial powder coating last outdoors?
A well-prepared polyester or super-durable system commonly lasts 10 to 20 years outdoors, depending on UV, salt and abrasion. A zinc-rich primer extends service life on steel in corrosive sites.

body: Powder coating surface preparation is the cleaning, pretreatment and masking work that decides whether a powder finish bonds for years or fails within months. At Koojo Custom Powder Coating, every part is degreased, chemically treated, rinsed and dried before any powder goes on. Since 2012, our Milton team has prepared more than 10,000 items for fabricators, manufacturers and contractors across the GTA, with a 48-hour turnaround. Whether you send raw steel weldments, machined components or aluminum brackets, our surface preparation for powder coating removes oil, residue and contamination so the coating can grip the metal. Request a quote below, or call (905) 876-7060, Monday to
Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM, and our team will advise on the right pretreatment for your parts.
Since 2012 | 10,000+ Items | 48 Hr Turnaround | Google Rating
## What Is Powder Coating Surface Preparation ?

Powder coating surface preparation is the sequence of cleaning, chemical treatment, masking and drying steps that readies bare metal for powder. It removes oils, oxides and soils, then leaves a clean, slightly reactive surface so the powder bonds firmly while it cures.

Powder cannot hide a dirty surface. Thermoset powder melts and flows in the oven at a cure temperature of 180–200 °C, so any film of cutting oil, forming lubricant or fingerprint residue trapped underneath causes craters, fisheyes and weak powder coating adhesion . Proper powder coating pretreatment solves two problems at once: it cleans the part, and it adds a thin conversion coating that improves grip and slows rust under the finish.

Without it, even premium powder can lift at edges and welds. That is why we treat surface preparation for powder coating as a core production step, never a cosmetic extra, and why every job at our shop begins here rather than in the spray booth. The powder is the visible finish, but the bond underneath decides how long it stays attached.
## How Does Our Powder Coating Pretreatment Process Work?

Our powder coating surface preparation has five stages: inspection and masking, alkaline cleaning , rinse, phosphate conversion treatment, and a final rinse and dry-off . Each stage removes one specific barrier to adhesion, and parts move to coating only when they are clean, dry and free of flash rust.

Inspection and masking (on arrival). We check each part for heavy rust, old coatings, weld spatter and trapped oil. We then mask threads, bores and contact faces with high-temperature plugs and tape. Masking for powder coating protects precision features, so bolts still thread in after curing.

Alkaline cleaning . A cleaning bath performs oil and grease removal from cutting fluid, shop dirt and handling marks. Degreasing before powder coating is the strongest defence against craters, so we never skip it, even on parts that look clean.
Rinse. Clean water flushes cleaner residue, which would otherwise interfere with the chemical treatment that follows.

Phosphate pretreatment . This step forms a thin crystalline layer on the metal. The layer improves grip and gives the finish a protected base. Metal pretreatment for powder coating always depends on the substrate and on where the finished part will live.
Final rinse and dry-off . A last rinse removes chemical salts. The rinse and dry-off step then drives off moisture, which is the key to flash rust prevention . Parts go straight to coating once dry.

Timing matters as much as chemistry. Every stage sits inside our standard 48-hour turnaround, and we receive parts Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Because multi-stage pretreatment happens first, coating and curing always start from a controlled surface. Our powder coating pretreatment is built into the schedule, not added afterwards, so a well-prepared part never waits on a separate booking. If your project has a deadline, tell us when you request a quote and we will plan around it. Clear communication at the start keeps powder coating surface preparation on schedule
and avoids surprises at pickup.
## Which Metals and Parts Need Surface Preparation for Powder Coating ?

Every metal needs preparation, but the method changes with the substrate. Steel needs oil and residue removed, aluminum needs its oxide layer controlled, and galvanized steel needs careful treatment and outgassing management. Fabricated and machined parts also need masking before coating.
Steel. Steel pretreatment targets mill oil, weld residue removal and early rust. It is the most common job we handle, and the metal pretreatment for powder coating we apply is matched to the part.

Aluminum. Aluminum pretreatment uses a chemical treatment that cleans the surface and builds a bonding layer, because raw aluminum oxidizes quickly. Here, the chemical treatment protects adhesion more than any other step.
Galvanized steel. Zinc surfaces respond differently from bare steel and can release trapped gases while curing, so galvanized parts get their own preparation plan.

Typical parts include welded frames, brackets, guards, railings, bollards, machine components and equipment housings. Each one needs powder coating surface preparation sized to its shape, because deep corners and enclosed sections trap oil and moisture more easily than flat plate. Our fabricated parts pretreatment and custom part preparation cover one-off pieces and repeat production runs, with the same standard applied to both. Good preparation means each load leaves with a production-ready surface , whatever the shape or size.
## What Pretreatment Options Does Koojo Offer?

Koojo matches the pretreatment to the part. Most steel receives a standard wash and phosphate sequence, aluminum and galvanized metal get a suitable chemical pretreatment , and parts with threads or sealing faces receive detailed masking. Heavy rust or old coatings are handled before pretreatment.
Standard pretreatment wash stages . Cleaning, rinsing, conversion treatment and drying for everyday steel parts, delivered as consistent powder coating pretreatment .

Iron or zinc phosphate. Iron phosphate pretreatment suits many indoor and general-duty parts. Zinc phosphate pretreatment is considered when a part needs extra rust prevention before coating , such as outdoor equipment.
Plugging and masking . Threaded hole masking , bore plugs and tape protect dimensions. Tell us about special requirements when you quote.

Heavy cleaning first. Thick rust, scale or an old finish needs more than a wash. Our sandblasting service removes it mechanically, and our restoration and recoating service handles aged coatings, before pretreatment begins.

Not sure which option fits? Send photos and the part material. We will recommend an approach, and our surface preparation for powder coating advice comes with your quote. Choosing the right powder coating surface preparation up front is far cheaper than fixing a failed finish later, and for aluminum and galvanized work we select the metal pretreatment for powder coating that suits that substrate.
## How Do We Check Pretreatment Quality?

We verify preparation through visual inspection, surface checks and adhesion testing on the finished coating. Koojo is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification, our inspection steps are documented, and test reports are
available on request, so you can trust the work behind every finish.

Pretreatment quality control starts before the bath: we look for oil, rust and weld residue on arrival. After rinsing, a clean surface should hold a continuous film of water, which is the idea behind the water break test . On the finished part, a cross-hatch adhesion test to ASTM D3359 shows whether the powder is gripping the metal.

Surface contamination is the most common cause of coating adhesion failure , and it shows up later as peeling and blistering . Catching it early costs far less than recoating. Strong powder coating pretreatment also keeps results consistent from batch to batch, and the same surface preparation for powder coating standard applies to every load. We hold our metal pretreatment for powder coating to the same documented checks, and powder coating surface preparation is never signed off until the part passes them. For the blasting cleanliness grades behind these checks, read our guide to surface preparation standards , and see our certification page for details on how we work. Our metal cleaning before powder coating is part of that documented process.
## See Surface Preparation in a Real Project

Welded frames arrive with weld residue, forming oil and tight tolerances, which makes powder coating surface preparation critical. Our conveyor frame case study shows what a documented job looks like for a real production customer, from the incoming part to the finished coating.

Read the conveyor frame for an automotive plant project to see the part, metal, size, powder, colour code and turnaround recorded for a real production job. Before and after photos show the standard we hold ourselves to, and the same documented approach applies to your parts.
## Which Industries Rely on Our Surface Preparation?

Fabricators, machine shops, manufacturers and contractors rely on us most. These customers need dependable industrial metal cleaning , tight masking and repeatable results that match the next batch. Our approach scales from single parts to production runs, and every customer receives the same careful treatment.

See how we support metal fabricators and welding shops , where weld residue is the main concern, and machine shops , where masking protects precision features. Our powder coating surface preparation also supports our wider industrial powder coating work, our metal pretreatment for powder coating on large fabrications, and the full range of powder coating services at our Milton shop.
## Get Your Parts Prepared Right

Ready for a stronger finish? Send part photos and details through our quote form for powder coating surface preparation advice, or visit 10874 Steeles Ave E, Milton, Monday to Friday, 7 AM to 5 PM. Call (905) 876-7060 or email sales@koojopowdercoating.com.
faqs: What happens if powder coating surface preparation is skipped?

Oil and residue stay under the powder, so the finish can crater, peel or blister, and rust can creep in from edges. Skipping surface preparation for powder coating usually means early failure and a costly strip and redo.
What is the difference between iron and zinc phosphate?

Iron phosphate forms a light conversion layer and suits general-duty indoor parts, while the right metal pretreatment for powder coating on outdoor equipment is often zinc. Zinc phosphate forms a heavier crystalline layer that offers stronger rust resistance for demanding or outdoor service.
Can you mask threads and holes?
Yes. We plug and tape threads, bores and contact faces before coating so they stay clean and in tolerance. Mark critical features on your drawing or photos when you request a quote.
Is pretreatment part of the 48-hour turnaround?
Yes. Powder coating pretreatment , drying and coating all fit inside our standard 48-hour turnaround for typical orders. Large or complex jobs are scheduled when we quote.

## The Challenge

## The challenge was to coat an automation line frame so it resists factory floor wear while its mounting plates, tapped holes and grounding points stay bare, flat and ready for equipment to bolt on without any rework at line commissioning .
That is why this automation line frame case study begins with what had to stay uncoated rather than with the colour.

An automated cell is only as accurate as the frame under it. Robots, vision sensors and fixtures bolt onto flat mounting plates , and any coating left on those faces can throw alignment off or stop a bracket from seating. Tight tolerance holes have the same problem, because powder in a thread or a dowel bore means drilling or tapping on site.

Electrical continuity added another layer. Automation equipment needs a clean path to ground, and a coated contact point breaks it. Grounding point masking therefore had to be planned on the drawing, not left to the person spraying. Getting that wrong on one frame would mean a call from the integrator during start-up, which is the risk this automation frame case study sets out to avoid.

Appearance mattered too. Machine builder frames are often built as modular frame sections that sit side by side, so every piece had to match the client's equipment colour standard . Batch colour consistency across the sections was part of the brief, along with a production schedule that left little slack for this automation line frame project .
## Our Approach

## Our approach in this automation line frame case study ran in three stages: masking and surface prep, an even electrostatic coat, and a cure followed by checks of every bare surface. The masking plan came first, because the bare surfaces decided how the rest of the job was run.
Preparation

We marked every mounting plate, tapped hole and grounding point on the drawing with the client before work began. Media blasting cleaned the welds and removed scale so the powder had a sound surface to bond to, and chemical pretreatment followed to improve adhesion and corrosion resistance. The frame was rinsed and dried fully before masking. On precision frames, masking often takes longer than spraying itself. Welds were also checked for porosity before blasting, since trapped air can cause pinholes during cure. Heat-resistant plugs filled the tight tolerance holes , and high-temperature tape covered the sensor mounting surfaces and ground pads. Careful prep is what turns an automation line frame into an install-ready frame .
Application

Electrostatic spraying carried the powder around tube corners and into gussets, giving weld seam coverage and edge coverage without heavy build on the flat faces. We set hang points away from visible surfaces and turned the frame during spraying so every side received the same film. Spray settings stayed the same for every section of the frame for an automation line , which keeps gloss and texture matched. Film build uniformity matters on modular frames, because a thicker coat on one section can show as a colour or gloss shift beside its neighbour on this automation line frame project .
Curing & Inspection

Curing ran at 180–200 °C on the thermoset powder supplier's oven cure cycle , in an oven rated for parts up to 6,000 lb. After cooling, we removed the masking and checked every bare surface for clean edges, with the drawing in hand so nothing was missed. Film thickness readings were taken to ASTM D7091 and adhesion testing was done to ASTM D3359, and the results sit in the job file. Those records keep this automation line frame case study traceable. Our usual 48 hour turnaround applies to standard work; the snapshot shows how long the automation line frame actually took.
## The Result

## The result was a powder coated machine frame with a smooth industrial finish , clean mounting plates and grounding points, open threads and recorded test readings, ready for the integrator to fit equipment as soon as the automation line frame arrived.

Because the masked areas stayed bare, robots and sensors could be bolted down and grounded without scraping or re-tapping. Even film build kept the frame square to the drawing, and the matched colour let it sit beside other sections without a visible change. That saves time at line commissioning , which is often the tightest part of an automation schedule.

The coating also protects the frame from the knocks, coolant splash and cleaning it will see over years of service. Old church gates usually carry several layers of paint, each one applied over the last whenever the metal started to show rust. Those layers crack, trap moisture and hide rust pitting underneath. Simply painting over them again would only restart the repaint cycle , with flaking back within a few seasons. Each layer added to the problem rather than solving it, and the gate leaves on these church gates were no exception.

Shape added the real difficulty. Decorative scrollwork , pickets and finials create recessed corners and tight gaps where powder struggles to reach, a problem known as the faraday cage effect . Without care, the outer curves get a heavy coat while the inside of each scroll gets almost none, and that is where rust returns first. For this church gates case study , fine detail coverage was the main test.

Function and appearance also mattered. Hinges, latch hardware and any moving parts had to swing freely after coating, and the finish had to respect the heritage appearance of the church grounds . The client also wanted a short gap between gate removal and reinstallation , so the church gates project had to keep moving through each stage.
## Our Approach

In this church gates case study the work followed three steps: strip and clean the metal back to bare steel, build the powder into every recess with careful spraying, then cure and inspect each leaf in good light before the gates went back to the church.
Preparation

Old paint removal came first. Layers that blasting alone would struggle with were stripped, and abrasive blasting then took the gates down to bare metal cleaning standard, opening up any rust pitting so it could be treated rather than hidden. We looked closely at every weld and scroll on the gates for a church for cracks or thin metal and flagged anything that needed repair before coating. Stripping also showed exactly how much original metal remained. A chemical pretreatment came next, followed by a rinse and a thorough dry. Hinge masking and masking moving parts finished the prep, so pins and latches would turn freely once the church gates were rehung.
Application

Detailed metalwork needs a different spray technique from flat panels. We lowered the gun settings and worked into the scrolls first, letting the powder settle into recessed corners before coating the outer faces, which beats the faraday cage effect without piling up film on the edges. Colour sample approval came before spraying: the client chose a satin black finish , a low gloss finish that reads as traditional ironwork. Each leaf of the church gates was hung so contact marks would sit on hidden edges, and the gate posts were coated in the same batch so the set matches.
Curing & Inspection

The leaves cured at 180–200 °C to the powder supplier's schedule, in an oven that takes pieces up to 6,000 lb. When they had cooled, we checked inside scrolls and behind pickets with a light, where thin spots would hide, then measured thickness to ASTM D7091 and adhesion to ASTM D3359, logging every reading for the church gates project . Masking came off last, and each hinge and latch was worked by hand to confirm free movement. ## The Result

The church received its ornamental gates back with a smooth, even finish deep inside every scroll and joint, hinges and latches that swing freely, a colour that suits the building, and test readings on file for the parish property records.

Because the coating on these church gates reaches the recesses as well as the outer faces, there are no thin spots waiting to rust through. That breaks the cycle of scraping and repainting that older wrought iron gates often fall into, and it gives the church outdoor durability measured in years rather than seasons. Maintenance drops to an occasional wash.

Visually, the low sheen hides small marks and keeps the gates close to the look of traditional ironwork. Visitors see clean, crisp detail on the finials and pickets instead of drips or heavy edges. The same restoration coating approach suits any church gates with fine detail, from a single garden gate to a full set of entrance leaves and posts. ## The Challenge

## The challenge was to give each safety bollard in the batch a high-visibility finish that stays bright under constant outdoor exposure , resists rust from road salt and survives knocks from vehicles, carts and snowplows for years without regular repainting.

Bollards work in one of the harshest settings a coating can face. Summer sun breaks down weak finishes and causes colour fade and chalking , while winter brings freeze-thaw cycles and salt spray from passing traffic. Once water gets under a chip, corrosion undercutting spreads beneath the coating and lifts it away from the steel. A safety bollard that turns rusty and dull also stops doing its job of being seen. Ontario sites see both extremes within the same year.

Impact is the other test. Vehicle impact from bumpers, shopping carts and snowplow damage all hit the same band near the top of each post, so the coating needs real toughness as well as weather resistance. Any weak point at the welds, the caps or the cut edges at the base would fail first. That is why this bollard powder coating case study begins with where the posts will stand.

Consistency mattered too. A row of posts outside a building is seen side by side, so every piece needed the same shade and gloss. The client also needed the posts back in time for site installation , so the schedule for this bollard powder coating project had to hold.
## Our Approach

## Our approach in this bollard powder coating case study was built around three steps: get the steel ready for years outdoors, spray a weather-rated powder, then cure and check each post before it went to site.
Preparation

We checked the drawing and the site specification with the client first, including the colour, the expected exposure and whether any posts were removable bollards with sleeves that had to stay uncoated. Abrasive blasting removed mill scale, rust and weld spatter from the steel pipe bollards and left a clean profile for the powder to grip. After chemical pretreatment and rinsing, each post was dried inside and out, including under the base plates. Posts with welded base plates need extra care at that joint, where water tends to collect. Drain holes were checked so water could not sit inside a post after installation. Where a project calls for extra corrosion protection, a zinc-rich primer can be added before the topcoat; whether this order used one is recorded in the specs. Careful prep is what keeps a safety bollard finish from lifting at the base.
Application

Powder choice comes first for outdoor work. For posts like these we use an outdoor polyester powder , a UV resistant powder type made to hold colour in direct sun, in the colour the client specified. Electrostatic spraying wrapped the powder around the pipe, over the welds and onto the bollard caps and base plates, with extra attention to cut edges . Each safety bollard hung from a point that would be hidden once installed, and the whole batch of matching bollards was sprayed with the same settings for a consistent colour match .
Curing & Inspection

The batch went through the oven together at 180–200 °C, timed to the manufacturer's data, and since the oven accepts loads up to 6,000 lb, long or heavy posts fit in one cycle. After cooling, each safety bollard was checked for full coverage and even colour. Thickness readings followed ASTM D7091, the adhesion test followed ASTM D3359, and both sets of numbers were filed with the order. Those records keep this bollard powder coating case study traceable. We quote 48 hours for standard work, and how long this bollard powder coating project took is noted in the snapshot.
## The Result

## The result was a set of safety bollards with a bright, even, weather-ready finish, full coverage over welds, caps and base plates, a consistent colour match across every post, and test readings on file, ready for site installation .

A low-maintenance finish like this cuts the cost of owning bollards. Instead of yearly scraping and repainting, the coating keeps rust out and stays visible through Ontario winters and summers. That matters for pedestrian protection , because a faded, rusty post is easy to miss at night or in snow. Each bollard powder coating project we finish is planned for that kind of service life.

The same standard applies to parking lot bollards , loading dock bollards and base plate bollards used for storefront protection .
